hints: Look at what each reagent does, one is a reducing agent and the other is an oxidising agent.
Remember that NaBH4 supplies hydrogen to the C=O bond, so both aldehydes and ketones can be reduced to alcohols.
Think about oxidation to a carboxylic acid, which needs a hydrogen still attached to the carbonyl carbon, so ask which type has that hydrogen.
walkthrough:
**What does NaBH4 do?**

NaBH4 is a reducing agent. It adds hydrogen across the C=O bond in carbonyl compounds.

Reduction reactions:
$$\text{RCHO} + 2[H] \rightarrow \text{RCH}_2\text{OH (primary alcohol)}$$
$$\text{RCOR'} + 2[H] \rightarrow \text{RCH(OH)R' (secondary alcohol)}$$

**What does acidified dichromate do?**

H+ / Cr2O7 2- (aq) is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids, and the orange solution turns green.

Oxidation reaction:
$$\text{RCHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}$$

**Why do ketones resist oxidation?**

An aldehyde has the group -CHO, so there is an H attached directly to the carbonyl carbon that can be replaced by OH. A ketone has the group C-CO-C with no such H, and breaking C-C bonds would be needed, which does not happen under these mild conditions. So ketones show no reaction with acidified dichromate.

**Put the row together**

With NaBH4: both react. With H+ / Cr2O7 2-: only aldehydes react. That matches the row for both react, only aldehydes react.

options.A: Incorrect. It is right that both react with NaBH4, but wrong to say both react with acidified dichromate. Ketones are not oxidised by H+ / Cr2O7 2- because they have no aldehydic H on the carbonyl carbon.
options.B: Correct. NaBH4 reduces both aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols. Acidified dichromate oxidises only aldehydes to carboxylic acids, while ketones show no colour change and no reaction.
options.C: Incorrect on both columns. NaBH4 reduces aldehydes as well as ketones, not ketones only. And acidified dichromate oxidises aldehydes only, not ketones.
options.D: Incorrect. It is right that only aldehydes react with acidified dichromate, but wrong to say only ketones react with NaBH4. Both types of carbonyl are reduced by NaBH4.
